# Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History

> > The Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History is a leading nonprofit organization dedicated to K-12 history education through primary sources, teacher professional development, and prestigious prizes including the Lincoln Prize and George Washington Prize.

The Institute offers comprehensive educational resources spanning colonial America through modern history, including MA degree programs, AP US History materials, and the History U online courses. Founded to improve history education, it maintains extensive collections, awards major book prizes for Civil War and founding era scholarship, and provides teacher training programs reaching educators nationwide.

## Key Topics

- American History Education
- Lincoln Prize and George Washington Prize
- Colonial America and Founding Era
- Civil War and Abraham Lincoln
- Slavery and African American History
- Teacher Professional Development
- AP US History Curriculum
- Primary Source Documents
- Master's Degree Programs
- Allen C. Guelzo and Civil War Scholarship
- Hamilton Education Program
- History U Online Courses
- Transatlantic Trade
- American Revolution
- David McCullough Essay Prizes

## Educational Programs and Courses

- [Period 2: 1607–1754 (AP US History)](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/ap-us-history/period-2): AP US History Period 2: Colonial America and British colonization resources
- [The American Civil War](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/masters-degree-american-history/courses/american-civil-war): MA course on Civil War by Allen Guelzo from Princeton University
- [History U | World War II](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/history-u/world-war-ii): History U self-paced WWII course by Michael Neiberg for high schoolers
- [Black Lives in the Founding Era](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/history-school/2021/black-lives-founding-era): History School 2021 course on Black history in founding era America
- [Voting Rights](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/community-college-civics-learning-guide/voting-rights): Community college civics guide on voting rights and suffrage history
- [Colonial America | Elementary Curriculum](http://www.gilderlehrman.org/curriculum/elementary/colonial-america): Elementary curriculum: Colonial America, Pilgrims, and Mayflower Compact
